name: Supreme Industries Ltd
title: Supreme Industries Ltd - 509930 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 volume rose about 12% to 753,907 MT while consolidated PAT fell 1% to Rs 954 crore; FY27 volume guided at 12-13%.
summary.overview: Supreme Industries reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 11,218 crore (up 7%) on volume growth of about 12%, with consolidated operating profit up 7% to Rs 1,654 crore and PAT down 1% to Rs 954 crore. Plastic piping volumes grew 14% while industrial products degrew 1% in volume and 3% in value. Management said the industry's plastic piping volume declined 9% in FY26 and guided FY27 piping volume growth of 15-17%, with overall growth of 12-13% and margins of 14-14.5%. PVC resin prices swung sharply in March (up about Rs 32-37/kg) and then fell about Rs 34/kg between 5 and 21 April, which management said was now corrected. Capex of about Rs 1,000 crore is planned, adding about 1.10 lakh MT of capacity to reach about 1.35 million MT per annum.

segments.name: Plastic Piping Systems
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 14% and value up 11%; management says the company retained leadership and is adding SKUs and systems (15,600+ SKUs across 45 systems, 1-2 more systems planned this year).

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: FY26 volume down 1% and value down 3%; management cited demand slowdown from OEM customers.

segments.name: Packaging Products
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 5% and value up 3%; a packaging facility is planned near JNPT on land not yet in possession.

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 4% but value down 1%.

segments.name: Wavin (acquired unit)
segments.commentary: Capacity 70,000 tons per year; plants running normally from February; Q4 volume about 10,000 tons; FY27 expected 48,000-50,000 tons. Plant was taken over in August 2025 and revamped for about 3-4 months.

segments.name: Windows and Profiles (Kanpur Dehat, UP)
segments.commentary: Production started 1 March 2026 with capacity around 10,000 windows per month; mature revenue potential of Rs 200-250 crore per year, invested more than Rs 200 crore; sales confined to UP and NCR.

guidance_outlook: FY27 piping volume growth guided at 15-17%; overall volume growth about 12-13% (management ranges per Q&A).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-14.5%, which management says yields more than 25% return on capital employed.

Planned capex of about Rs 1,000 crore including carry-forward commitments, adding about 1.10 lakh MT capacity (1,00,000 MT piping, 10,000 MT material handling), to be added by FY27, partly operational by March 2027 and fully in about two years.
Wavin volume expected at 48,000-49,000 tons in FY27 at about 70% utilisation of 70,000 tons capacity.
No inventory gain expected in Q1 FY27 given the PVC price fall; management sees no further PVC price erosion for now due to a weaker rupee (about Rs 94.5/USD).
Management said the Nal Se Jal and Jal Jeevan funding is uncertain; it expects industry plastic piping volume growth of about 8% in FY27 per raw material producers.
Long-term aspiration to reach 2 million tons volume (from about 1.35 million MT installed capacity); export plastic piping business is about $5 million, with a target of $50 million.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of about Rs 1,000 crore for the year including carry-forward commitments, adding about 1.10 lakh MT, taking installed capacity to about 1.35 million MT per annum.
Four plants described on the call to be partly operational by end-March 2027 and fully operational in about two years; land already in hand.
Packaging facility planned at JNPT, pending land possession; capex not yet quantified.
Gas piping: capacity about 10,000 tons per month spread across 9 plants; orders received from 3-4 gas companies, with more under negotiation.
Windows and profiles: about 10,000 windows per month capacity at Kanpur Dehat; Kanpur Dehat expansion to follow once capacity is sold.
Utilisation: management considers 70-75% good utilisation; Q2 is a seasonally lean period and utilisation may be 68-70% in weaker conditions.
demand_pricing: Management said PVC prices fell about Rs 34/kg (about 30%) from 5 to 21 April 2026, after rising about 32% in March; current PVC price cited at about Rs 81/kg.
Management said channel inventory at distributor and retail levels is mostly cleared after the price correction; the company declined to quantify Q4 channel inventory or monthly volume trends.
Agri demand was hit in March by the steep price rise, with farmers deferring purchases; management expects strong agri demand from Q1 FY27 after crop harvest in April.
Management said India imports about 68% of PVC requirement, with China supplying a large share and the Middle East disruption affecting polyethylene more than PVC.
Management said there is no shortage of PVC, PP or polystyrene in India.
Management said industry plastic piping volume declined 9% in FY26 and expects about 8% growth in FY27.
CPVC volume grew about 38% in FY26 (volume only, value not disclosed); CPVC share of piping was not disclosed.
Management said the company's piping market share is about 12-13% outside CPVC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook for piping and overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Piping volume growth of 15-17% and overall volume growth of 12-13%, with margins of 14-14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in Q4 or Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No inventory gain for full FY26; Q4 net inventory gain around Rs 70-80 crore; no gain expected in Q1 as PVC prices are falling.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 1.10 lakh MT capacity addition is in piping?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1,00,000 MT in piping and 10,000 MT in material handling systems, all to be added by FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses stay flat in Q4 despite higher volume?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there was no one-off; repairs and advertising were controlled from Q3, and FY26 publicity spend was Rs 98 crore versus Rs 125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise sharply in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said assets capitalised from prior-year capital work in progress of more than Rs 400 crore; closing CWIP is Rs 136 crore; total FY26 asset additions Rs 1,400 crore including Wavin.

qa_highlights.question: Is government spending on Nal Se Jal or Jal Jeevan picking up?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; management said central funds depend on state matching contributions, and only about one-third of budgeted spend was achieved in the last two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin and how is it defined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management's stated criterion is return on average capital employed above 25%, which it says has been achieved for 18 years; it sees 14-14.5% margins as delivering that.

risks_watch: PVC resin price volatility: about Rs 34/kg fall in April after a March spike; management expects no further erosion, but volatility is structural.
Channel inventory and Q1 demand: management declined to disclose month-wise or April channel data.
Government water-scheme (Jal Jeevan, Nal Se Jal) funding remains uncertain; management said it is not sure of spend this year.
Export moderation from geopolitical and tariff disruption; Middle East supply shock affecting polymer feedstock.
Industrial products segment faces OEM demand slowdown; FY26 value down 3%.
Wavin ramp-up toward 48,000-50,000 tons and Windows business reaching Rs 200-250 crore revenue depend on utilisation; timing not specified.
Depreciation step-up from capitalisation of new assets will weigh on margins.
Management is reticent on disclosure (channel inventory, PVC inventory days and cost, CPVC revenue share, gas-pipe market size), limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and capex plans, but evasive on quantitative detail: management repeatedly declined to share month-wise volumes, channel inventory, PVC inventory cost and CPVC revenue share. Cautious on government water-scheme funding and geopolitics, while describing demand as recovering from Q1 FY27.
key_quotes: So we do not anticipate now any price reduction also because rupee is getting weaker, rupee is around INR94.50.
We not only make piping systems from PVC, CPVC and also polyethylene also.. So believe that 14%, 14.5% margin will give a return in excess of 25% on capital employed.
There is no uncertainty. We look forward to achieve 2 million tons.

Wavin acquired unit, 70,000 t/yr capacity, running normally from February 2026
Windows and profiles plant at Kanpur Dehat, ~10,000 windows/month, production started 1 March 2026

growth.why: FY27 overall volume guided at 12-13% and piping volume at 15-17%, with margins 14-14.5%; backing is partial: 1.10 lakh MT capex (partly live by March 2027, full in ~2 years), Wavin ramp to 48-50k t and Kanpur windows plant, but industry piping volume is guided at only ~8% and no order book is quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-14.5%, but FY26 consolidated operating profit of Rs 1,654 crore on Rs 11,218 crore revenue is about 14.7%, and depreciation is stepping up from Rs 1,400 crore of asset additions, so margins are guided flat to slightly lower, not expanding.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: partly by March 2027; full in about 2 years
rows.why: About 1.10 lakh MT (1,00,000 MT piping, 10,000 MT material handling) is under construction on Rs 1,000 crore capex, taking installed capacity to about 1.35 mn MT; land is in hand and Wavin is ramping to 48,000-50,000 t from 70,000 t capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 overall volume guided at 12-13% and piping at 15-17% versus industry piping volume guided at only about 8%, with FY26 volume already up about 12% to 753,907 MT.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rs 1,000 crore capex for FY27 including carry-forward commitments is already committed, with the packaging plant at JNPT pending land possession and capex not yet quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management sees no inventory gain in Q1 FY27 after the Rs 34/kg PVC fall, and Q2 utilisation may drop to 68-70% in weaker conditions, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Channel inventory was not quantified, government water-scheme funding is uncertain (only about one-third of budgeted spend achieved in the last two years), and industrial products fell 3% in value on OEM slowdown.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 1-2 more piping systems this year on top of 45 systems and 15,600+ SKUs, and the Kanpur Dehat windows plant (about 10,000 windows/month, Rs 200-250 crore mature revenue potential) started 1 March 2026.

rows.label: PVC price correction and no further erosion
rows.why: PVC fell about Rs 34/kg (about 30%) from 5 to 21 April after a roughly 32% March spike, now about Rs 81/kg; management expects no further erosion given a weaker rupee at about Rs 94.5/USD, but PVC volatility is structural and no inventory gain is expected in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Gas piping orders from 3-4 gas companies
rows.why: Gas piping capacity is about 10,000 t/month across 9 plants with orders from 3-4 gas companies and more under negotiation, but no order value is quantified.

rows.label: Agri demand rebound after channel destock
rows.why: Agri demand was hit in March by the steep price rise, management says channel inventory is mostly cleared, and it expects strong agri demand from Q1 FY27 after the April harvest, though it declined to quantify channel inventory.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15-17% piping volume guide, the Rs 1,000 crore capex and the 14-14.5% margin target, but was evasive on channel inventory, PVC inventory cost and CPVC revenue share; analysts probed other expenses flat in Q4, depreciation step-up and government water-scheme funding.
